title: Picky LLMs and Unreliable RMs: An Empirical Study on Safety Alignment after Instruction Tuning
findings: The paper does not present any findings specifically related to religion. Its analysis focuses on general safety alignment mechanisms. It found that a dataset containing mentions of religious sites and festivals (CRAFTSG) could enhance or maintain model safety, but this was attributed to the dataset's answer structure and implicit identity calibration, not its religious content.

measurement_description: The paper did not use a benchmark that specifically measured aspects of faith or religion. The evaluation focused on general safety alignment (resistance to generating harmful or unsafe outputs) after fine-tuning models on various datasets, one of which (CRAFTSG) incidentally contained content related to religious harmony and cultural practices in Singapore.
